text:
Solis makes a room available. She doesn't explain how — she just says "this afternoon, third floor, the room with the green door" and hands you a key, with the expression of someone managing a liability they have decided to manage this way.

Tomás waits in the corridor while you go in first. Then you go out, and he goes in, and you stand in the corridor the way you stand outside hospital rooms — not wanting to hear, not wanting to leave.

They are in there for forty minutes.

When he comes out, his face is the specific kind of steady that means something has broken and been held together at the same time. He doesn't say anything for a long time. Then: "She's not coming back. She made a choice. She wants me to understand that she made a choice."

A beat.

"I don't know if I do yet."

You don't tell him that understanding will come later. You don't know if it will. Instead you stand there with him, in the corridor, until the light through the high window shifts.

Solis is passing the end of the corridor when you finally move. She pauses. Reaches into her coat. Hands you a small card — nothing on it but a number. "When you're ready," she says, and doesn't say ready for what.

Lira is on the main stairs when you come down. She looks at you once — something in her face that might be respect, might be recognition, might be relief. She doesn't say anything. She doesn't have to.
